clue.text: Book from writer and explorer

blocks.note: Katherine Mansfield, the New Zealand short-story writer
Mungo Park, the Scottish explorer of the Niger

explanation.surface: A volume penned jointly by an author and an adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two surnames, one of a writer and one of an explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel of 1814 is a well-known example of a book.

clue.text: Maiden belongs to organized group? That's not true

definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a synonym

blocks.note: M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over
something that belongs to a set is in it
a formation is an ordered arrangement of people or aircraft

explanation.surface: A young woman joins a club, or perhaps that is only a rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden over, with no runs scored, is marked M.
explanation.definitionFit: Misinformation is false or misleading information, the kind of report one would call untrue.

clue.text: Coward holding one end of bomb for explosives expert

indicators.note: an end of a word is its first or last letter, here the first
holding something means having it inside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: Noel Coward, the playwright
the opening letter of bomb

explanation.surface: A frightened person clutching a bomb waits for the bomb-disposal man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person; it is the playwright Noel Coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite and made his fortune manufacturing high explosives.

clue.text: Stories like this are made up with falsity

indicators.note: made up means invented or composed, so the letters are put together in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Such stories are invented and untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a plain comment on lies; 'are' and 'falsity' together hold exactly the ten letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales are traditional children's stories of magic, and also a byword for invented untruths.

clue.text: Horsehide?

blocks.note: surface padding: the two meanings are written run together as one word
first meaning: the unbeaten 18th-century English racehorse
second meaning: to obscure, as the moon covers the sun

explanation.walkthrough: 'Horsehide' looks like leather; split in two it is a famous horse and a verb for concealing.
explanation.definitionFit: The racehorse Eclipse was never beaten, and to eclipse something is to block it from view.

clue.text: Cashier put out of office

blocks.note: first meaning: to discharge an officer from the armed forces in disgrace
second meaning: to remove from a job or post

explanation.surface: A bank teller is sacked from their post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like a bank clerk; here it is the verb for discharging someone in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss is to sack or discharge someone from employment, as cashiering does to an officer.

clue.text: Foreign churchman born in Lincoln

indicators.note: placed in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president
B is the abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: A priest from abroad who was born in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' looks like the English cathedral city; it is Abraham Lincoln, known as Abe.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French title for a priest or cleric, so a churchman from abroad.

clue.text: It may be terribly keen, if e.g. sharpened finally

definitions.text: It may be terribly keen, if e.g. sharpened finally

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are jumbled
finally points to the very last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
the closing letter of sharpened

explanation.surface: A blade's cutting side is extremely sharp once it has been honed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer and describes it: a well-sharpened blade is very keen.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutting side of a blade is honed to be keen, and a well-sharpened one is very sharp indeed.

clue.text: Experimental means to give one a rise after retirement?

definitions.text: Experimental means to give one a rise after retirement?

blocks.clueFragment: Experimental means to give one a rise after retirement?
blocks.note: surface reading: a trial scheme to boost a pensioner's income
setter's reading: going to bed at night, so the thing that rises is a piece of bedroom furniture, and the experiment was a 1950s vertical take-off test rig

explanation.surface: A trial pension scheme to raise income after one stops work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' and 'rise' suggest pensions and pay; read them as going to bed and lifting off. The nickname was given to Rolls-Royce's 1950s jet-lift test rig.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolls-Royce Thrust Measuring Rig, an experimental vertical take-off craft, was nicknamed for its bed-frame look.

clue.text: Special sets built - foreign films may need them

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a synonym

indicators.note: something special is out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A film studio constructs special sets for its pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special sets' reads as film scenery; 'Special' is the signal and 'sets built' supplies the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Translated captions along the bottom of the screen let viewers follow dialogue in a language they do not speak.

clue.text: Fish beginning to bite at head of stream

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
placed at the head means put in front, so the first piece comes before the second

blocks.note: the opening letter of bite
a rill is a small brook or stream

explanation.surface: An angler's fish starts nibbling up where a stream begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A brill is a European flatfish related to the turbot, sold for the table.

clue.text: Sea-bird fed by royal command

blocks.note: first meaning: a sailors' name for the giant petrel
second meaning: Nell Gwyn, whom Charles II on his deathbed asked should not be left to starve

explanation.walkthrough: Charles II's last words are reported as 'Let not poor Nelly starve', a royal command that his mistress be provided for.
explanation.definitionFit: The pet form of Nell Gwyn's name, and also a sailors' term for the giant petrel of southern oceans.

clue.text: Painter of illustrations for mug

blocks.note: first meaning: pen name of Hablot K. Browne, who illustrated Dickens
second meaning: slang for the face

explanation.surface: An artist is commissioned to decorate a drinking cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a drinking vessel to paint; here it is slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for physiognomy, it is old slang for the face, and was also Browne's signature on his Dickens drawings.

clue.text: Paper's omitted leader backing the House

indicators.note: a leader left out means the opening letter is dropped from the word
going backwards means reading the remaining letters from right to left

blocks.note: The Times, the newspaper this puzzle appears in

explanation.surface: A newspaper drops its editorial in favour of supporting the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the House' suggests Parliament; it is just a house. A semi is a semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a semi is a semi-detached house, a very common type of suburban home.

clue.text: Correct approach, you'll find, in this puzzle corner

blocks.note: right means correct
an angle is a way of approaching a problem

explanation.surface: Advice that the right method will be found in a corner of the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: Every corner of a square crossword grid is a ninety-degree turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The corners of a square grid each form a ninety-degree turn, which is the geometric term.

clue.text: Don't be intimidated by striking clock

blocks.note: workers on strike are out
slang: to clock someone is to see their face, and clock is also slang for the face

explanation.surface: Advice not to flinch at a chiming or punching clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' reads as a clock chiming, or as hitting; here it means on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To outface someone is to stare them down or defy them boldly instead of backing off.

clue.text: Vulgar column included by foreign press organization

indicators.note: something included by another is held within it, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: TASS was the Soviet news agency
a stele is an upright stone slab or pillar

explanation.surface: A crude newspaper column is printed by an overseas news agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' suggests a newspaper feature; it is a stone pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tasteless shows poor judgement and lacks refinement, which is what vulgar means.

clue.text: A cut of beef to enjoy in festive gathering

blocks.note: shin is a cut taken from the lower leg
slang: to dig something is to like it

explanation.surface: Tucking into a joint of beef at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Crime producing young female fatality announced by Scot

indicators.note: a Scot saying the words out loud gives a spoken version, the clue wants that pronunciation

blocks.note: a girl is a miss, and deid is the Scots for dead, a fatality

explanation.surface: A girl's death turns out to be a crime, reported by a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots, dead is pronounced 'deid', so a young woman who has died is a 'miss deid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeed is a wrongful act or offence, so it can stand for a crime.

clue.text: Revolutionary end Reds achieved in China

indicators.note: a revolution turns things upside down, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A communist revolution ends with Reds in power in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is porcelain, and the capital C hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is the fine porcelain made at Meissen near that German city, so it is a kind of china.

clue.text: Sportsman allowed to enter heat, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word may be one of several arrangements of its letters
entering something means going inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the letters of heat rearranged
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A competitor is cleared to run in a qualifying heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heat' looks like a race heat; it is only the four letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person who competes in sports, especially track and field.

clue.text: An obsession about the left in Parliament

indicators.note: going about something means around it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A fixation on left-wing politics among members of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the left' suggests the political left; it is only the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Althing is Iceland's national legislative assembly, among the oldest in the world.

clue.text: Opponents of US, including the British spy chief

definitions.note: the US is read as the pronoun us

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the head of the British secret service in the Bond novels

explanation.surface: America's enemies, among them Britain's head of espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make US look like America; read it as the pronoun us, whose opposite side is the other lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'us and them' idiom sets one group against the other, so the other side are opponents.

clue.text: Over the side

blocks.note: first meaning: remaining, as in food that is spare
second meaning: one of the two sides, the opposite of right

explanation.surface: Something tipped over the side of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover food is what remains, and the word is also the name of the port or sinister side.

clue.text: Organize assembly in a state

blocks.note: taken as written
the abbreviation for Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Arranging a gathering of people somewhere in a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' suggests a condition or nation; it is an American state, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather things or people together into a heap or collection.

clue.text: Group of stars regularly appearing in airliners

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters of airliners

explanation.surface: A star cluster that is often seen from aeroplanes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is a constellation of the zodiac, a recognised pattern of stars.

clue.text: Sort of story used in picture after picture

blocks.note: first meaning: a long heroic narrative
second meaning: the word studios have applied to film upon film, Hollywood's big spectaculars

explanation.surface: A kind of tale that turns up in one film after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half looks like a description of where the story appears; it is how the word is used to sell big films.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative of heroic deeds, and the label is stuck on grand-scale Hollywood spectaculars.

clue.text: Parts of Open University, in short, having an advantage

indicators.note: split into parts, the letters are broken up and put back in a different order

blocks.note: the institution's name shortened to its first word and initial

explanation.surface: Some courses at Britain's distance-learning university give students a head start.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university; 'in short' trims it to the five letters that are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one up means holding a slight lead or edge over a rival.

clue.text: Performance great physician put on inside

definitions.note: adverb, in prison; the answer is a verb phrase meaning serving a sentence there

indicators.note: one thing put on another is added to it, so the pieces are joined end to end

blocks.note: a doing is an act or performance
the proverb says this heals all wounds

explanation.surface: A doctor's show is staged within a hospital or theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time is the great physician' is an old proverb; 'inside' is slang for in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone serving a jail sentence is said to be inside, behind bars.

clue.text: Another visitor, we hear, criticized with hindsight

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so the sound of the words matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: a further visitor is a second guest

explanation.surface: A second caller at the house is judged harshly after the event.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'second guest' runs into the past tense of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To second-guess a decision is to criticize it after the outcome is already known.
